processes.title: Business function chart
processes.building: This screen is being built in Slice 1.
processes.subtitle: Five levels, coded automatically · each process step owns exactly one business requirement
processes.noChildOfProcess: A process step has no children.
processes.empty: No functions yet. Start with a level-1 function.
processes.reorderHelp: Move a function up or down among its siblings — every code below it is renumbered in one save.
processes.pickNode: Select a function in the hierarchy to see and edit it.
processes.notInTree: That function is not in the chart. It may be retired — turn on Show retired to see it.
processes.newLevel: The new function sits at level {n}. Its code is generated from the parent chain on save.
processes.addProcessHelp: A process step gets its business requirement at once. A level-5 function is always a process.
processes.name: Function name
processes.promoted: Now a process step — requirement {br} created.
processes.retireBody: {name} is hidden from the chart. It can be restored from Show retired. A function with live children or a live requirement cannot be retired.
processes.staleAction: Someone else changed this first. It has been reloaded — try again.
processes.staleLink: Someone else changed this first. It has been reloaded — try again.
processes.noEntities: There are no data entities yet.
processes.noParties: There are no external parties yet.
processes.noOrgRoles: There are no org roles yet.
processes.edgeOtherHelp: Leave empty for the start or end of the flow.
processes.edgeFixed: {from} → {to}. To join different steps, remove this flow and add a new one.
processes.conditionRequired: A conditional branch needs a condition, e.g. “Credit check failed”.
processes.conditionHandoff: For a hand-off with no next step, name who receives it.
processes.flowGapsHelp: Gaps in the flows of the steps under this node.
processes.gap.orphan_steps: Steps with no flow in or out
processes.gap.no_lane: Steps with no Responsible role (no swimlane)
processes.flowPageHelp: The steps under this node, in swimlanes by their Responsible role.
processes.flowCanvasHelp: Click an arrow to edit, move or delete it. Click a box to rename or retire the step. Drag from a box's blue dot onto another box to add a flow. Drag a box to place it; the position is saved.
processes.flowCanvasHelpReadOnly: You can view this flow. Your role on the project does not allow changes to it.
processes.flowNoSteps: There are no process steps under this node yet.
processes.resetLayoutBody: Every saved position on this diagram is removed and the boxes are arranged automatically. Flows and steps are not changed.
processes.suggestFailed: The arrows could not be suggested.
processes.suggestBanner: Suggested arrows, in chart order: start, each step in turn, end. Nothing is saved until you keep them. You can change any arrow afterwards.
processes.addStepHelp: The step is added to the chart under this node, with its business requirement. Connect it by dragging from its right edge.
processes.edgeNoEnds: A flow needs at least one step.
processes.edgeMoveNote: Changing a step removes this flow and adds a new one with the same type and condition.
processes.deleteEdgeConfirm: Delete this flow? It can be added again later.
processes.dfdPageHelp: The one process diagram (D-38): each lane is who performs the steps in it, and the steps run left to right in the order their data gives — a step comes after the step whose output it reads. Stores, outside parties and triggers sit below.
processes.dfdCanvasHelp: Drag a box to place it; the position is saved. Click a step to open it in the chart, where its data is edited.
processes.dfdCanvasHelpReadOnly: Click a step to open it in the chart. Your role on the project does not allow moving boxes.
processes.dfdNoSteps: There are no process steps under this node yet.
processes.dfdNoFlows: No step under this node has data in or out yet. Add it on a step in the chart.
processes.dfdCrossAreaHelp: Written in one top-level area of the chart and read in another.
processes.dfdLegend: Rounded box: process step · Cylinder: data store · Heavy square: outside party · Circle: trigger (double ring: time)
processes.mermaidHelp: Copies this diagram as Mermaid text, to paste into a document or a slide tool that renders Mermaid.
processes.mermaidCopied: Mermaid text copied to the clipboard.
processes.mermaidFailed: The Mermaid text could not be fetched.
processes.mermaidManualHelp: This browser did not allow copying to the clipboard. Select the text below and copy it.
processes.retireStepTitle: Retire this step with its requirement and flows?
processes.retireStepBody: {name} is hidden from the chart and the flow, together with everything below that exists only because of it.
processes.retireStepLoading: Checking what goes with this step…
processes.retireStepSummary: {br} and its data links ({data}), roles ({roles}), outside flows ({outside}) and arrows ({arrows})
processes.retireStepSummaryNoBr: Its data links ({data}), roles ({roles}), outside flows ({outside}) and arrows ({arrows})
processes.retireStepNothing: Nothing else is attached to this step.
processes.retireStepBlocked: Something outside this step still depends on it. Retire these first:
processes.retireStepUndo: One click brings it all back: Restore with its requirement and flows, from Show retired. The data entities, org roles and outside parties themselves are not retired.
processes.retireWithDependents: Retire with its requirement and flows
processes.retiredWithDependents: Step retired with its requirement and flows.
processes.restoreWithDependents: Restore with its requirement and flows
processes.restoredWithDependents: Step restored with its requirement and flows ({n} records).
processes.restorePlainFits: This step was retired on its own, so it is restored on its own. Press Restore.
processes.restoreDependentsFits: This step was retired with its requirement and flows, so it comes back with them. Press Restore with its requirement and flows.
processes.restoreFirstTitle: Nothing was restored. These are still retired — restore them first:
processes.subtitleAsIs: The as-is chart: how the work is done today · as-is steps carry no business requirement
processes.emptyAsIs: The as-is chart is empty. Start it by copying the to-be chart, or add a level-1 function.
processes.chart.label: Which chart
processes.chart.copyFrom.TO_BE: Copy the to-be chart into this one
processes.chart.copyFrom.AS_IS: Copy the as-is chart into this one
processes.chart.copyPreview: This copies {nodes} nodes ({processes} process steps), {data} step data links and {triggers} triggers, with their performers and supporting systems. As-is steps carry no requirements.
processes.performer.title: Performed by
processes.performer.help: Who or what does this step: a department, a position, an IT system or an AI. Where the DFD is used, it is the step's lane.
processes.performer.none: No performer yet — on the DFD the step sits in the Unassigned lane.
processes.performer.aiHint: Saves when you press Enter or leave the field.
processes.performer.toBeWarning: This IT system is marked to-be, but it performs a step of the as-is chart.
processes.trigger.title: Started by
processes.trigger.help: A time (month-end) or an event (a customer calls) that starts this step. A trigger counts as the step's input.
processes.trigger.pick: A trigger already in this project
processes.trigger.name: Trigger name
processes.trigger.newHint: Saves when you press Enter or move on. Esc drops it. A name the project already has adds that trigger.
processes.gapsHelp: Each step needs what this project's DFD rule asks for (Settings → Components). While this chart's DFD is used, such a gap blocks the baseline freeze.
processes.gapsRuleOff: This chart's DFD is not used on this project, so these gaps do not block a freeze.
processes.dfdGapHelp: This step misses an element of the project's DFD rule. It blocks the baseline freeze.
processes.dfdGapsAlert: {n} steps below this node have a gap that blocks the baseline freeze — see the steps marked 'gap'.
processes.dfdShowOrder: Show the order (derived from the data)
processes.chart.copyPreviewToBe: This copies {nodes} nodes ({processes} process steps), {data} step data links and {triggers} triggers, with their performers. It creates {requirements} new draft requirements, one per process step.
processes.dfdCounts: {steps} steps · {stores} stores · {parties} outside parties · {triggers} triggers · {flows} flows
processes.dfdNoData: No data in or out yet.
processes.dfdUsedBy: Steps that use it (In / Out of the step)
processes.dfdInspectHelp: Click a box to see its details here; double-click a step to open it in the chart, where its data is edited. Drag a box to place it; the position is saved.
processes.dfdInspectHelpReadOnly: Click a box to see its details here; double-click a step to open it in the chart. Your role on the project does not allow moving boxes.
processes.dfdList.title: Data flow diagrams
processes.dfdList.subtitle: Drawn from the processes, the data they read and write, and who performs them. Wider diagrams of a higher level open from the function chart.
processes.dfdList.heading: {n} diagrams
processes.dfdList.empty: There is no diagram yet: a data flow diagram appears when a function in the to-be chart has process steps below it.
processes.dfdList.emptyAsIs: There is no diagram yet: a data flow diagram appears when a function in the as-is chart has process steps below it.
processes.dfdList.goChart: Go to the business function chart
processes.savedNodeOnly: Function saved. The requirement was not saved — see its message.
processes.savedBrOnly: Requirement saved. The function was not saved — see its message.
processes.panel.unmakeProcess: Stop treating this as a process…
processes.panel.logicPlaceholder: The rules it applies, and what happens when they fail
processes.panel.outputPlaceholder: What exists when it is done
processes.panel.descriptionInfo: What this function is for. On a process it sits under Description, beside Data processing.
processes.panel.dataProcessingInfo: How the process handles its data, in prose. It moves into the requirement's structured lines in a later release; this text is kept.
processes.promoteBody: {name} becomes a process step. This is what happens:
processes.promote.br: A business requirement is created and numbered at once. The number is never reused.
processes.promote.noChildren: The box can no longer hold sub-steps.
processes.promote.undo: Undoing it means retiring that requirement first.
processes.promote.freeze: While this chart's DFD is used, a process with no input or no output blocks the next baseline freeze.
processes.promote.asIs: As-is steps carry no business requirement: who does it, its data and its parties are recorded on the step.
processes.demoteTitle: Stop treating this as a process?
processes.demoteBody: {name} stops being a process step. This is refused while the step still has a live requirement, data, roles or parties.
processes.run.title: How it runs
processes.run.savesAsYouGo: each change saves on its own
processes.run.info: Text you type above (the name, description and other fields) waits for Save — the counter shows how many changes are unsaved, and Ctrl+S saves too. Everything under How it runs saves the moment you change it: choosing the performer, adding or removing a trigger, ticking roles and data. A name you type here (an AI performer, a new trigger) saves when you press Enter or move on. Done just closes the editor.
processes.run.noOthers: No R, C or I yet
processes.save.refused: Not saved — see the message above
processes.leave.title: Save your changes first?
processes.leave.body: {name} has {n} unsaved changes. Save them before moving on, or discard them.
processes.leave.body_one: {name} has 1 unsaved change. Save it before moving on, or discard it.
processes.run.draft: Name not saved yet — open and press Enter
processes.run.dfdOnly: On the diagram, not in the requirement yet
processes.run.noBrDataButDfd: Nothing on the requirement yet — the data below is recorded on the DFD only. Add an entity and tick what the requirement does with it.
processes.run.dfdOnlyInfo: Drawn on the DFD, or added by an external flow or a chart copy. Pick C, R, U or D for it in the grid above to make it part of the requirement.
processes.leave.draft: A performer or trigger name still being typed under How it runs is discarded too.
processes.save.draftOpen: Press Enter in the performer or trigger name to save it first, or Esc to drop it.
processes.dfdLight.label: DFD readiness
processes.dfdLight.tipReady: Ready: everything the DFD needs is recorded for this process.
processes.dfdLight.stillNeeded: Still needed to complete the DFD:
processes.dfdLight.element.STARTED: Something that starts it: a trigger, a data input, or an inbound external party
processes.dfdLight.notReadyOnlyInfo: Shows every process that is not Ready, with the functions above it: red ones miss an element of this project's DFD rule and block the freeze; yellow ones meet the rule but miss a recommended element.
processes.dfdLight.allReady: Every process in this chart is ready.
processes.dfdMark.label: DFD
processes.dfdMark.element.STARTED: any one of: a trigger, a data input, or an inbound external party
processes.dfdMark.element.DATA_OUT: at least one data entity out
processes.dfdLight.element.ORDER: Joined to another process through its data
processes.dfdLight.element.EXTERNAL: An outside party on its diagram
processes.dfdLight.recommendedMissing: Meets this project's rule. Recommended, not yet recorded:
processes.dfdMark.element.DATA_IN: at least one data entity in
processes.dfdMark.element.ORDER: joined to another process through its data
processes.dfdChartOrderHelp: No step reads data another writes yet, so the steps stand in the order of the function chart. The order appears by itself once the data joins them.
processes.dfdList.noPartyHelp: This project's DFD rule asks for at least one outside party on each diagram. Until one is recorded on a process below, the freeze is refused.
processes.draw.already: Already on the diagram — nothing was added.
processes.draw.refusedSelf: A step cannot hand data to itself.
processes.draw.refusedTrigger: A trigger only starts a process step: draw from the trigger to a step.
processes.draw.refusedPair: That is not a data flow. A line joins a step to a store, an outside party, a trigger or another step.
processes.draw.handOffTitle: Hand data to the next step
processes.draw.handOffHelp: {from} writes the data entity, {to} reads it. The order arrow between them follows from this.
processes.draw.dropHelp: Choose the data entity {step} reads or writes. A store new to this diagram is placed where you dropped the line.
processes.draw.newHelp: It gets its DE- number when saved.
processes.draw.noCrud: The requirement's data use (C, R, U or D) is not filled in from the diagram — pick it on the step.
processes.draw.partyIn: {party} sends data into {step}. Name the data entity, or give the flow a label.
processes.draw.partyOut: {step} sends data to {party}. Name the data entity, or give the flow a label.
processes.draw.removeBody.EXTERNAL: Remove this flow between {step} and the outside party:
processes.draw.removeHelp: Order arrows are not removed here: they follow from the data and change when the data does.
processes.draw.noFlows: No step under this node has data in or out yet. Drag from a step's right-hand dot to a store, another step or empty space to draw one.
processes.draw.inspectHelp: Click a box to see its details here; double-click a step to open it in the chart. Drag from a box's dot to draw a flow: it is saved as the step's data, as on the step. Click a flow to remove it. Drag a box to place it; the position is saved.
processes.guide.what: “{name}” is a business function: a heading that groups the work below it. The requirement, who does the work, what starts it and the data it uses are written on a process, not here.
processes.guide.below: {n} processes sit below it. Open one to describe it.
processes.guide.below_one: One process sits below it. Open it to describe it.
processes.guide.tooHigh: Processes start at level {n}. Add a box below this one, then make that box a process.
processes.guide.noneBelow: Nothing below it is a process yet. Open a box below it and make that box a process.
processes.guide.make: If the work is done at this level, make this box a process.
processes.starts.where: Input data and inbound outside parties start a process too. They are recorded under Data and External parties, and on the DFD — this list only shows them.
processes.starts.none: No input data and no inbound outside party.
processes.starts.nothing: Nothing starts this process yet: no trigger, no input data and no inbound outside party.
processes.volume.title: Volume
processes.volume.needs: Hours and FTE appear once these are filled in: {what}.
processes.volume.basis: One FTE = {days} working days × {hpd} h = {per} h a year
processes.volume.onSave: the figures update when you save
processes.volume.conflict: Someone else changed this process first. Discard and look again, then re-enter your figures.
processes.vsum.title: Time & FTE
processes.vsum.subtitle: Annual hours per business area, today beside the change — the time the change saves. Only processes with all their figures are counted.
processes.vsum.basis: One FTE = {days} working days × {hpd} h = {per} h a year.
processes.vsum.noAsIs: There is no as-is chart yet, so nothing to compare against. Start one from the business function chart.
processes.vsum.noneMatched: No area matches on both charts at this level yet.
processes.vsum.hint: Areas are paired only when both their code and their name agree on the two charts.
processes.vsum.unmatchedHelp: These areas are shown on their own and never added into the time saved.
processes.vsum.reason.CODE_SAME_NAME_DIF: The same code holds a different name on the other chart (renamed?)
processes.vsum.reason.NAME_ELSEWHERE: Same name under {code} on the other chart — probably reordered
